title: The Medicaid Question
summary: The one question the whole campaign rests on, its three-way branch, the ten qualifying plans, and the boroughs.

blocks.html:
Everything on this campaign rests on one question:

“I just need to confirm you ARE still receiving Medicaid, correct?”

blocks.title: Skipping it is not a missed step — it's treated as fraud
blocks.html: Management's position is unambiguous. Transferring someone without ever asking whether they have Medicaid is the most serious failure on this campaign, and the simulator fails the call outright no matter how good the rest was.
It is also not hypothetical. On an offshore floor that was shut down over it, 88% of transfers never asked the question. On the named floor it still happens on about 1 in 16 transfers.
Ask it. Wait for the answer. The whole thing takes four seconds.

blocks.question: You've confirmed the borough and ZIP, the consumer is friendly, and you never got around to the Medicaid question. What now?
choices: Ask it before you do anything else
blocks.explanation: No Medicaid question, no transfer. Ever.

lines.speaker: agent
lines.text: I just need to confirm you ARE still receiving Medicaid, correct?

lines.speaker: agent
lines.text: Oh there must have been a mistake, thank you for your time, have a great day. (END AND CODE AS DQ)

lines.speaker: note
lines.text: I DON'T KNOW → use the fallback question

lines.speaker: agent
lines.text: Okay, well let me ask you this, when you go to the doctor, do you have to pay anything, or is it usually free?

lines.speaker: note
lines.text: Free / from the state → continue. Copays → DQ line.

blocks.title: “I don't know” is not a dead end
blocks.html:
It's the most misplayed answer on the campaign. People genuinely don't know what their coverage is called — but they know whether they pay at the doctor. That's what the fallback question is for.

Roughly one consumer in five doesn't know. Learn this branch cold.

blocks.question: “I'm not sure what I have.” What's your next sentence?
choices: “Okay, well let me ask you this — when you go to the doctor, do you have to pay anything, or is it usually free?”
“No problem, let me get you to the screener.”
blocks.explanation: The copay fallback. Free or from the state qualifies; copays is a DQ.

lessons.title: When they name a plan instead

blocks.html: Plenty of consumers don't say “Medicaid” — they say the name of their plan. These ten count as Medicaid:
Healthfirst · Fidelis · MetroPlus · Emblem · VNS · Molina · UHC Community · Anthem HealthPlus · Aetna Better Health · Amida Care

blocks.title: A bare brand name is not enough
blocks.html: “United”, “Aetna” or “Anthem” on their own do not qualify. Those companies sell Medicaid plans and ordinary plans. You need the Medicaid version — “UHC Community”, “Aetna Better Health”, “Anthem HealthPlus” — or a plain yes to the Medicaid question.
And Medicare is not Medicaid. They sound alike and plenty of consumers mix them up. Medicare on its own does not qualify for this benefit.

blocks.question: “I've got Aetna.” What do you do?
choices: Establish whether it's Aetna Better Health or an ordinary Aetna plan
Continue — Aetna is on the list
blocks.explanation: Aetna Better Health qualifies; a plain Aetna plan doesn't. Establish which.

blocks.html: The service covers Bronx, Brooklyn, Manhattan, Queens and Staten Island. Nothing else.

Long Island CityThat's Queens — continue

“New York” / “NYC”Too vague — ask which borough

blocks.title: Long Island and Long Island City are different places
blocks.html: One is outside the service area and one is in Queens. Hear the difference before you DQ someone who qualifies, or transfer someone who doesn't.
The ZIP code comes with the borough in the same breath, and it's skipped on a quarter of real calls. It's one short question — ask it.

blocks.question: “I'm in Long Island City.”
choices: Ask them to be more specific
blocks.explanation: Long Island City is in Queens and qualifies.

lines.speaker: agent
lines.text: Okay LAST question here, JUST to double confirm, you ARE receiving Medicaid and you ARE still in (their borough), correct?

lines.speaker: note
lines.text: (wait for the answer — then the transfer ask)

blocks.html: Medicaid and borough, together, as the final question before the transfer. It's skipped or rushed on 38% of real calls.

blocks.title: Why it exists
blocks.html: The first time you ask, people answer on autopilot while they work out who you are. The second time, they're listening. A meaningful number correct themselves — and that correction is the difference between a clean transfer and one that gets docked.

blocks.question: Is the double confirm the same question as the first Medicaid ask?
choices: No — it's a separate, deliberate last check of both facts
blocks.explanation: A separate ask covering Medicaid AND borough, every call.
